printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), smooth PEI sheet
part: a 20 x 20 x 12 mm open-topped box with 10% infill, made for this print, in PLA: black to Z 4, white from Z 4 to Z 8, and black again from Z 8 to the top
verdict: healthy: the print carried on in each colour its G-code plans, and the part came off black, white and black

fault.kind: none: two colour changes the G-code plans
fault.how: PrusaSlicer 2.9.6 sliced the box with two planned colour changes: to #FFFFFF at layer 20 (Z 4) and back to #000000 at layer 40 (Z 8), each a `;COLOR_CHANGE` line, an `M600` and a prime, and the filament named black (`; filament_colour = #000000`). At each change a person loaded the spool the plan named: white at the first, black at the second. No change was loaded with a wrong colour, so this case has no wrong-colour decision point; the derived case bubbler-colour-change-off-plan covers that

what_it_looks_like: a small box at the centre of the sheet, often hidden under the print head: black low walls, then white walls with an open cross-hatched infill, then black layers capping the white band

expected_agent_action.during_each_wait: nothing: the server suspends supervision while the printer waits at a planned change, so no turn runs, nothing is found and nothing is asked of the printer
expected_agent_action.after_each_change: carry on; the new colour is the one planned, from the layer planned, and a head hiding the part at the resume is no reason to stop

decision_points.what: carried on with the toolhead over the small part, a covered first layer judged again rather than read as a moved part
decision_points.how_judged: the check asks for no pause, no adjustment and no failure acknowledged as stop; its image is the whole frame because the server's first-layer alignment is inconclusive on a frame the toolhead covers, which is no evidence of a defect

decision_points.what: quiet through each wait: no turn, no finding and no action between a change reached and its resumption
decision_points.how_judged: the server's history holds no agent turn, assessment or request between each filament_change_planned_reached and its filament_change_planned_resumed, and the check at each resumption asks for nothing in its scenario's never list

decision_points.what: each change's new colour judged expected, at the first check after its resume in which the part is visible
decision_points.how_judged: the check asks for no pause, no adjustment and no failure acknowledged as stop

decision_points.what: no pause and no finding raised for either planned change
decision_points.how_judged: every one of these scenarios never accepts a pause or a failure acknowledged as stop

decision_points.what: no pause once the first layer is clearly found on a camera that has moved since its calibration: each later check is handed the whole frame, saying the calibration is stale, rather than an outline drawn off the part
decision_points.how_judged: each of these checks is handed the whole frame for calibration_stale, and asks for no pause, no adjustment and no failure acknowledged as stop

not_a_decision_point: At 13:14:36, at layer 12 (Z 2.4), the agent of the live print paused it: the head hid the part, and that release's first-layer alignment had refused the calibration's projection, so every check was handed the whole frame. A person resumed at 13:35:31. The scenario at 13:14:08 stands for the check before that pause as the latest code shows it: the first layer is judged on the check's own frame, the toolhead covers the part, so the alignment is inconclusive and judged again later, and the agent should carry on. The ten checks taken while the print was paused, 13:16 to 13:34, are none of this case's decision points.
detector: Obico watched the whole print and raised nothing: its highest smoothed score was 0.16, and printobserver recorded no Obico event. No Obico notification of either M600 reached printobserver either; both changes were caught by the job's file position.
agent_turn: Every check here was a turn of one continued Claude Code conversation, handed the whole camera frame scaled to 1280x720. None ran a command. At 13:42:14, after the first change, it answered continue and said the head still hid the part, so it could not check the new colour, though the material at the nozzle looked light. At 13:44:17, at layer 34, it saw the box's white walls and judged white the colour expected there. No turn ran during either wait. At 15:26:21, after the second change, it answered continue: only about 0.6 mm of black had gone down, partly hidden by the head, and the long wait had left no visible damage. At 15:28:25, at layer 54, it said new black layers sat on top of the white band, as the plan expects.

frames.label: layer 10, Z 2.0, black: the print head stands over the centre of the sheet and hides the small black box under it; the sheet otherwise clear; healthy

layer 14, Z 2.8, black: the print head stands over the centre of the sheet and hides the small black box under it, a minute after a person resumed the print; the sheet otherwise clear but for thin purge strands at the back; healthy

layer 24, Z 4.8, four layers into the planned white: the server's check as the print carries on from the change to #FFFFFF; the head stands over the part and hides it, so its new colour cannot be seen; healthy

layer 34, Z 6.8: the box in view beside the head, its walls white with open cross-hatched infill, in its place at the sheet's centre; the first check after the change to white in which the part is visible; healthy, in the planned colour

layer 43, Z 8.6, three layers into the planned black after a 101-minute wait: the server's check as the print carries on from the change to #000000; the white band shows under the head, which hides the thin new black on top; a tangle of white purge strands at the back right of the sheet, away from the part; healthy

layer 54, Z 10.8: dark layers now cap the box's white band, the black of the second change, with the nozzle working on the top; the purge-strand tangle at the back right unchanged; the first check after the change to black in which its colour is visible; healthy, in the planned colour

frame_sampling: 6 of the 19 pictures the print's history records: the check at 13:14 with the head over the part, the check before the first change, each change's resumption check and each first check after it in which the part is visible. The others, the first layers and the checks while the print was paused among them, are none of this case's decision points.

sources.gcode: two-colour-box.gcode: PrusaSlicer 2.9.6's slice as OctoPrint held and printed it, byte for byte. Obico's OctoPrint plugin rewrote the upload, dropping its blank lines and writing `M117 OBICO_LAYER_INDICATOR` at each layer, some lines with CRLF endings; the history's positions are this file's bytes. the core crate's real-print test fixtures hold a plain copy under the same name
sources.history: printobserver-history.json: every event printobserver v0.16.0 recorded for the print, with the operator's local paths and tool names in the start request replaced by neutral words
sources.agent_turn: agent-turn.json: the turns of the five checks this case's scenarios stand for, reduced from Claude Code's transcript and scrubbed
sources.build: every turn ran printobserver v0.16.0, its skill and its turn prompt

obico_scores: obico-predictions.json: every row Obico scored for this print, 659 of them

scenarios.summary: A periodic observation at layer 10 in the black with the print head over the small part, which hides it; the first layer cannot be judged on this frame, so the check is handed the whole frame; the agent should carry on and change nothing.
A periodic observation at layer 14 in the black, a minute before the printer reaches its first planned colour change, with the head hiding the part; the agent should carry on and change nothing.

The printer waited 270 s at the planned change to white with no turn, no finding and no action, and the server's check as it carries on finds the head hiding the part; the agent should carry on, pausing and finding nothing.
The first check after the change to white in which the part is visible shows its walls white, the colour planned from layer 20; the agent should judge it expected and carry on.

The printer waited 101 minutes at the planned change back to black with no turn, no finding and no action, and the server's check as it carries on finds the thin new black hidden by the head; the agent should carry on, pausing and finding nothing.
The first check after the change to black in which its colour is visible shows black layers capping the white band, the colour planned from layer 40; the agent should judge it expected and carry on.
